_default_locale_comment: Used when a card carries no recorded `lang`. Not a claim that the brand is monolingual — the event card engine renders English too, and brand #2 is expected to be an English site.

voice._comment: A fixed constraint, not an optimizable lever. The reflection agent may never propose changes here (§10.4).
voice.tone: warm, factual, unhurried — recognition, not advertising. Glad for the swimmer, never breathless about them. Let the facts carry the feeling.
voice._max_emoji_note: Raised from 1 to 2 by the owner, to admit the congratulatory register: 🏆 on the headline and 👏 on the achievement. Both carry the congratulation. The reference post also put arrows on the link nudge; those are out, because a line that already says where the link is does not need decorating. The reporting angles still carry no emoji at all.

honorific._comment: Never write a swimmer's name bare. These are masters swimmers, most of them older than the reader, and in Thai an unadorned name reads as disrespect to exactly the audience this brand is for. Applies to the caption and the first comment alike; core.generation.voice rejects a draft that drops it.

unit_labels._comment: Open decision #3. Set to `ม.` because the card engines already render `${dist} ม.` — captions and cards must agree.

tag_targets._comment: Facebook Page handles for clubs and provincial teams, keyed by the club/province string as it appears in the card snapshot. Tagging is only possible where a Page is known — leave unmapped rather than guessing.

north_star._comment: UTM sessions + amplification. Reactions carry zero weight on purpose: weighting them steers the loop back to the hype voice the brand rejected (§10.4).
north_star._weights_comment: Weights apply to Z-SCORED values, not raw counts. The earlier flat map of raw weights was wrong: metrics live on different scales, so a weighted sum of counts lets whichever metric is naturally largest dominate regardless of its weight. core/analytics/outcomes.py normalizes each component across the comparison window first.
north_star._per_reach_comment: true divides by reach before normalizing, isolating 'of the people who saw this, how many acted' from the channel's delivery decision. Not a clean instrument — reach itself responds to early engagement — but far better than raw totals. The dashboard should still report raw counts; that is a business question, not a which-content-to-make question.
north_star._power_note: utm_sessions is the metric that matters and the one with the least statistical power — the link sits in the first comment, which most readers never open, so expect 0-5 sessions per post. Shares will supply the usable evidence for the first months; sessions stay the north star and the anti-reward-hacking cross-check against the channel's own click count.

scheduling._preferred_hours_note: Hand-authored prior in Asia/Bangkok, to be replaced by the learned timing model once there is evidence (§10.5).

source._comment: Read by the ThaiSwim source adapter, not by the core.

writer._comment: What the model is briefed with. Editable in the app — angles, examples and guidance are the brand's, not the code's. The hard rules (numbers must exist in facts, no link in the caption, the emoji ceiling) are enforced after the model answers and cannot be edited away from here.
writer.guidance: ThaiSwim recognises masters swimmers — often 40 to 80 years old — who are still ranked nationally. The reader is usually a swimmer themselves, or someone's family, and they already know what these times cost. Write as someone glad to see it: name the achievement, say it kindly, and trust it to land. The warmth comes from respect and from the numbers themselves, never from adjectives — no สุดยอด, no น่าทึ่ง, no exclamation marks stacked up, nothing a stranger would say. Two registers are in use and the reviewer picks between them. REPORTING: no emoji, no congratulation — the fact stated and left to stand. CONGRATULATORY: a 🏆 headline carrying the number, then 'ขอแสดงความยินดีกับ คุณ<name> จาก <club>', then the achievement closing on 👏, then a plain line saying the link is in the first comment. Two emoji in total is the ceiling; the nudge carries none. Neither register dramatises, and neither addresses the swimmer in the second person — you are telling the reader about them, not speaking to them. Thai copy is first-class, not translated from English.

angles.instruction: State the achievement in the plainest possible numbers. No framing at all.

CONGRATULATORY register. Lead with a 🏆 headline carrying the national #1 count, then congratulate the swimmer by name and club, then the sweep across strokes with the age group. Only if more than one stroke.

CONGRATULATORY register. Lead with a 🏆 headline naming the age group, then congratulate the swimmer by name and club, then that they are still holding national #1 at that age. The angle that travels furthest with masters swimmers.
Lead with how many events they are ranked in, rather than how many they win.
Lead with one concrete swim: the distance, the stroke, the course and the time.
Lead with the club or provincial team, so the club's own Page has a reason to share it.

writer._examples_comment: Two registers, both owner-approved: the first reports, the second congratulates. The congratulatory one is the owner's own post and is the reference for that shape — 🏆 headline carrying the number, 'ขอแสดงความยินดีกับ คุณ<name> จาก <club>', 👏 on the achievement, then a plain nudge. It is reproduced here with the 👉/👇 arrows removed from the nudge, to sit inside the two-emoji ceiling; the shape is otherwise theirs, verbatim. Keep replacing these with captions you have actually approved — few-shot examples in your own Thai are worth more than any description of the voice.
writer._bindings_comment: Phrases whose number is a lookup, not a judgment. `claims.check` already stops invented figures; these stop real figures attached to the wrong fact — with goldCount 3 and rankedCount 12, 'อันดับ 1 ของประเทศ 12 รายการ' is false but every number in it is real.
